text:
Hi all,
I’d like to consult with anyone here whose partner recently registered as an exempt business (osek patur).

We read online that if I accompany him to the tax authority, I should be able to sign on his behalf without any problem. However, when we got there, we were told that if I wanted to sign for him, we would need a notarized power of attorney, which is fairly expensive.

We're wondering whether it's worth trying again at the same office. Our appointment was at the end of the day, and perhaps they didn't have the patience to look into whether there was a way to make it work without a notary.

Has anyone here been able to do this without a notarized power of attorney? If so, is there a legal basis for it?

Thanks!
